lessons.title: Lesson 1 – Introduction to Life’s Purpose (1 hour)
lessons.content:
Session 1 – Introduction to Life’s Purpose (1 hour)

Key Topics

  • Key Topics:

Activities

  • Activity: Reflective journaling—“When did I feel most alive and fulfilled?” journalize

Additional Notes

  • rebuilding of St. Paul's Cathedral after a fire burned through London in 1666.
  • An architect was visiting the project site and loved to interact with those doing the
  • work and approached three bricklayers. He asked them each individually, "what
  • are you doing?".
  • The first bricklayer replied, "I'm a bricklayer. I'm working hard to lay bricks to
  • earn money so I can feed my family." The man seemed tired and wasn't as far
  • along with his work as the others.
  • The second bricklayer says, "I'm a builder. I'm building the finest, strongest wall.
  • This wall will be a foundation for this building and will protect everyone who is
  • inside."
  • The third bricklayer replied with energy and a light in his eye, "I'm a cathedral
  • builder. I'm building a great cathedral, where people can gather, pray and
  • celebrate the Almighty."
  • This is a demonstration that everything we experience is based on our
  • understanding of purpose and depth of vision. Everything is "an inside job." How
  • we interpret what we do, or experience, is based on the purpose of the action and
  • the actor, for the actor's mindset reflects on purpose.
  • •
  • o What is life's purpose? 7 Questions for Clarity:
  • 1. What makes you feel most alive?
  • 2. What problem in the world gets you most emotionally charged?
  • 3. What are you naturally good at?
  • 4. What is your life's most meaningful event or experience?
  • 5. What would you do if you had zero fear?
  • 6. Who is your idol, living or dead, and why?
  • 7. What do you want to be your enduring legacy?
  • Answer the foregoing questions sincerely, for therein lies the discovery of your purpose.
  • o Difference between goals, vision, and purpose.
  • 1. Purpose begets vision
  • 2. Vision begets goals
  • 3. Purpose: The reason for which something is done or created or for which
  • something exists. Your purpose is the reason for your being.
  • 4. Vision: An act or power of anticipating which will or may come to be –
  • giving direction for the outcome of goals and purpose
  • 5. Goals: specific, desired outcomes that guide actions and effort towards a
  • particular predetermined end
  • o Purpose-driven lives: Gandhi's nonviolence, Mandela's fight for justice,
  • Mother Teresa's compassion.
  • Gandhi, Mandela and Mother Teresa are shining examples of lives well lived with
  • purpose. Gandhi left his law practice behind and focused on liberating Asia and
  • Africa from the yolks of colonial rule. He often took expeditions to South Africa
  • to fellowship with the who were engaged in freedom struggle.
  • His crown jewel of endeavor came in the form of relentless non-violent resistance
  • against British rule of his nation, India. He summed it all in the following thought.
  • "The main purpose of life is to live rightly, think rightly, act rightly. The soul
  • must languish when we give all our thought to the body." Mahatma Gandhi
  • Mandela's purposeful find for the liberation of his nation landed him in much
  • trouble, and he was imprisoned and even labelled a terrorist among other things. It
  • was his purpose that fueled his staying power. And he stayed the course until he
  • birthed a rainbow nation out of Apartheid.
  • "For to be free is not merely to cast off one's chains, but to live in a way that
  • respects and enhances the freedom of others." – Nelson Mandela
  • Mother Teresa's life in Calcutta and beyond touched the world in a manner most
  • special. Her compassion lingers on years after her demise. She did not only
  • contribute to the assuaging of pain, but she also took part in it due to a purpose
  • greater than herself.
  • "Help the poor while living among them, sharing their experience and treating
  • them with kindness, compassion and empathy, but never pity." – Mother Teresa
  • Napoleon Hill's 17 Success Principles Lists Definiteness of Purpose as the top attribute in
  • ensuring achievement.

lessons.learning_objectives: Objective: Understand the concept of purpose and why it matters.

quiz.title: Lesson 1 – Introduction to Life's Purpose (1 hour) Quiz
quiz.description: Quick check on core ideas from this lesson.

questions.question_text: Purpose provides a long-term direction that informs goals and actions.
questions.explanation: Purpose is the overarching 'why' that guides decisions.

questions.question_text: Vision is the same as a daily to-do list.
questions.explanation: Vision describes a desired future; tasks are immediate actions.

questions.question_text: A clear purpose makes prioritization among competing tasks easier.

questions.explanation: Specific, time-bound goals are trackable and actionable.

questions.question_text: Match each concept to its definition. (A–C with 1–3)
